title: Wild Leopards & Untamed Coastlines
summary: Immersive expedition for wildlife photographers and conservation enthusiasts. Private trackers, custom open-sided 4x4 safaris, and private coastal yacht charters for sperm and blue whale sightings.

cover.alt: Open-top safari jeep watching a leopard on a granite boulder in Yala

description:
Privileged leopard tracking in Yala and Wilpattu, secluded glamping pavilions, and azure whale migrations off Mirissa. This is the journey I design for travellers who measure a day by the light — dawn and dusk drives, long patient waits and the thrill of a leopard stepping out of the scrub.

Between the parks we slow down: Udawalawe’s elephant herds, Bundala’s flamingos and, to finish, a small private yacht out to the blue whale highway off the southern coast.

overview.heading: Three National Parks and the Blue Whale Highway
overview.quote: A good safari is mostly silence: the engine off, the tracker listening for a langur’s alarm call, and then a leopard walking out of the shade as if it owned the morning — which it does.

days.title: Arrival & Into the Lakes of Wilpattu
days.description: From the airport we drive north along the coast to a tented camp on the edge of Wilpattu, Sri Lanka’s largest national park. Late-afternoon safari among its natural lakes, the villus, looking for leopards and sloth bears.

details.label: Overnight Residence
details.value: Luxury tented camp near Hunuwilagama gate

days.title: A Full Day in Wilpattu’s Wilderness
days.description: Dawn and dusk drives with a picnic breakfast beside a villu. Wilpattu sees a fraction of Yala’s visitors, so sightings are quiet and unhurried — leopards, sloth bears, spotted deer and crocodiles basking on the banks.

days.title: Across the Island via the Gem Town of Ratnapura
days.description: A long but scenic transfer south, broken with lunch in Ratnapura, the city of gems, and a look at traditional gem pits. Evening arrival at Udawalawe.

days.title: Udawalawe Elephants & Onward to Yala
days.description: A dawn drive among Udawalawe’s grazing elephant herds and a visit to the Elephant Transit Home at feeding time, then on to a tented camp on the edge of Yala for a sunset drink by the waterhole.

days.title: Yala: Leopard Country from First Light
days.description: We enter at gate opening with a senior tracker and stay out until late morning, then return in the afternoon — exploring quieter blocks so that every sighting is calm and engine-off.

details.label: Private 4x4
details.value: Modified open vehicle for your party only

days.title: Bundala Flamingos & the Road to Mirissa
days.description: An early birding walk at Bundala’s salt pans — flamingos, painted storks and waders in season — then west along the coast to a beach villa in Mirissa. Afternoon free.

days.title: Private Yacht to the Blue Whale Highway
days.description: Out at sunrise on a small private yacht with a marine naturalist to look for blue and sperm whales and spinner dolphins. The afternoon is for the beach, the pool or a sunset at Coconut Tree Hill.

details.label: Season Note
details.value: Whales Nov – Apr; dolphin and coastal cruise outside the season

days.title: Coastal Expressway & Airport Farewell
days.description: A relaxed breakfast by the sea, then the expressway north to the airport. A Galle Fort lunch stop can be added for later flights.

details.label: Option
details.value: Lunch and a walk in Galle Fort for evening flights

reviews.title: Patience, silence and four leopards
reviews.text: We are keen wildlife photographers and have done safaris in Kenya and India. Dinesh and his tracker had the same patience as the best guides we know: engine off, no shouting between jeeps, and a long wait at a waterhole in Wilpattu that ended with a female leopard walking past twenty metres away. The blue whale morning off Mirissa was the perfect finale.

related.title: The Grand Ceylon Odyssey
related.summary: The quintessential Ceylon masterpiece. Climb Sigiriya at sunrise before the heat, wander sacred tooth relic temples, traverse the tea mountains on the vintage observation train, and track leopards in Yala.

cover.alt: Tea train crossing the Nine Arch Bridge in Ella in morning light

related.title: Pristine Southern Beaches & Whale Trails
related.summary: Five unhurried nights along the southern coast — Galle Fort’s ramparts, a cinnamon island boat safari, stilt fishermen at sunset, blue whales off Mirissa and secluded coves near Tangalle.

cover.alt: Golden crescent beach in Tangalle with palms and stilt fishermen at twilight

related.title: Tea Mist, Monasteries & Colonial Charms
related.summary: Slow down with gentle high-altitude air, artisanal tea tastings with fifth-generation estate managers, private evening prayers at the Temple of the Tooth, and misty walks between colonial planter bungalows.

cover.alt: Colonial tea estate bungalow among misty emerald tea terraces near Hatton
